definitions.gloss: perforation; line of small holes for tearing
definitions.explanation: A row of small holes or cuts in paper or packaging that allows a section to be torn off cleanly. Common on envelopes, receipts, stamps, tickets, and forms.

examples.japanese: ミシン{目|め}に{沿|そ}って{切|き}り{取|と}ってください。
ミシン{目|め}が{入|はい}っているので、{手|て}で{簡単|かんたん}に{切|き}り{離|はな}せます。
examples.english: Because there are perforations, you can easily tear it off by hand.

examples.japanese: この{応募|おうぼ}はがきはミシン{目|め}で{本体|ほんたい}から{切|き}り{離|はな}してお{送|おく}りください。
examples.english: Please tear this entry postcard along the perforations and send it.

notes:
ミシン comes from ミシン (sewing machine, from English 'machine'), as the line of small holes resembles stitch holes made by a sewing machine needle. The {目|め} component means hole or eye.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ミシン{目|め}に{沿|そ}って: along the perforations
- ミシン{目|め}で{切|き}り{取|と}る: to tear off along the perforation
- ミシン{目|め}を{入|い}れる: to perforate
